scaling.note: ROOM 2 DECLARES ITS OWN DEPTH, from its own architecture. height = 0.369 x (y - 300), anchored on two measurements of the plate that agree to the pixel: the saloon porch deck is 40px for about 0.6m and its batwing doorway 134px for about 2.0m, and both imply a 1.75m man at 117px at the building line. Errata 54’s shared zones (222/240/263) belong to Room 1, whose street is shallower; applying them here puts a man at 1.66 times the height of the door he walks through. Doc 36 Q10.

gilt.note: Act III. Doc 05 Part Two-B: 'Fresh gilt on the lettering. Business is good. Business, for the Company, is always the search, and the search just outlived its most annoying obstacle. Me.' say: Half of it is two stories tall in front and one story deep.
The other half is real, and is doing better.
onEnterSay.note: His first sight of the town, and the words come from doc 05's THE FALSE FRONTS rather than being written fresh -- he has the opinion already; this is him having it out loud at the moment he first has it. AMENDED AFTER TYLER CHECKED IT AGAINST THE PLATE: the original said EVERY building was a false front, which the picture contradicts -- the saloon is a flat parapet with a low roof behind it, and the hotel beside it is genuinely two storeys with lit windows and real depth. The plate is signed off, so the writing yields, and the observation is better for it: the half that is real is the half with money, which is the town's whole economy in one line. Gated on T_SEEN_MAIN_STREET, which onEnter sets, so it plays once.

obstacles.note: A thing on the ground he must walk around. Thad walked through the trough because the walk bands are full-width quads and nothing in them says otherwise. The rect is the trough’s own hotspot rect -- one truth, not two.

lamps.note: The Nugget’s open doors, the brightest thing on the street.
The lantern hung for the map seller. A single flame, so it moves more than a doorway.
The Improvement Company’s windows. Steady: they can afford good oil.
